decisions.reason: As a design-oriented devore decoration fabric line close to the firm's core textile know-how, it is likely to be retained because the firm can learn from customer feedback and refine variants, although collection turnover in decorative fabrics raises some discontinuation risk.

This transparent burnout decorative fabric line fits the firm's established decoration textile capabilities and service model, so absorptive capacity argues for continuation, but its fashion-sensitive character makes it somewhat more likely to be replaced than a staple item.

Because this burnout decorative fabric is close to the firm's existing offer, management can interpret market signals and improve or reposition it, which supports keeping it unless demand proves clearly weak.

A velour-like upholstery fabric builds directly on the firm's upholstery business and stocked-supply strengths, so it benefits from strong related knowledge and is relatively unlikely to be withdrawn quickly.

The flame-retardant plain inbetween fabric extends the established range in a technically adjacent and commercially useful way, making it a good candidate to keep given the firm's continuity and service-focused positioning.

This polyester lining fabric with satin sheen is a close extension of the firm's core interior textile assortment, so the firm is likely to retain it as a complementary product supported by existing sourcing, warehousing, and customer relationships.
